title: Repair metric-index skew and reconcile trace linkage during multi-tenant failover
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Summary:
During a recent regional failover/switchover event we observed a correlated set of customer escalations reporting missing dashboard tiles (tenant-specific time series) and broken trace-to-request linking. Root cause analysis points to two related failures: a shard/tombstone propagation lag that caused metric index skew for affected tenants, and a router prefix-cache invalidation bug that resulted in trace ID pointers being written to an outdated trace-index partition. The net effect: dashboards returned empty or partial series and trace explorer failed to stitch spans for 30-90 minutes for affected tenants (hosted and Dedicated pools).

Impact:
- Several high-value customers reported partial or missing metrics (application latency, token usage) and inability to correlate traces to UI events.
- Console dashboards showed 0-values or 'no data' for tenant-scoped widgets for the failover window.
- Observability SLO alerts were noisy due to missing series and caused paging for oncall.

Root cause details:
1) Metric-index skew: when tenant allocation moved between ingest shards during failover, tombstone markers and per-tenant watermark updates were not propagated atomically; some shards short-circuited and dropped recent writes during reindexing. This left the metrics-timeseries index with gaps and orphaned series.
2) Trace linkage break: the routing prefix cache used to choose trace-index partitions was evicted during failover but not rebuilt quickly for a subset of request paths; subsequent writes used an older partition mapping and trace ID references were placed where the trace-stitcher did not expect them.
3) Contributing factor: backpressure behavior in the write path caused amplified reordering of writes under transient load, exposing both issues simultaneously.

Proposed fix (phases):
Phase A - Immediate mitigation (hotfix, canary):
- Patch router to use a versioned prefix-map fetch with fallback to master mapping (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123). This prevents tracing writes from landing in stale partitions.
- Add a small synchronous confirmation step during tenant move so tombstones are acknowledged across all ingest replicas before completing the move.
- Deploy hotfix to canary cluster (us-west-2) and run the repair steps below against a subset of affected tenants.

Phase B - Repair and backfill:
- Run a controlled metric backfill that replays write-ahead logs (WAL) for tombstoned windows to reconstruct missing series. Script: https://git.internal/redwood/scripts/repair/replay-metrics-backfill.sh
- Reindex trace pointers for a sliding window of the incident by scanning write logs and restoring trace-link entries into the correct partition.
- Validate by comparing per-tenant series counts and percent of trace links successfully stitched pre/post backfill (target >99%).

Phase C - Hardening and automation:
- Add a pre-move barrier in the tenant-migration service ensuring tombstone and watermark propagation (unit + integration tests).
- Add monitoring: 'tenant-metric-count-delta' and 'trace-link-stitch-rate' per-tenant with alert thresholds and runbook links.
- Add bench test that simulates failover and validates metric continuity and trace linking.

Rollout plan:
- Canary (us-west-2) for Phase A only: 2026-03-11 - 2026-03-12 (completed for router patch in canary).
- Phase B backfills run 2026-03-12 - 2026-03-14 for 12 impacted tenants; estimated 36 hours total work with throttling.
- Global rollout of Phase A hotfix: 2026-03-14 after validation.
- Phase C hardening merged into mainline and scheduled for release in runtime-1.24.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added for prefix cache refresh logic and tenant-move barrier.
- Integration test harness extended to simulate WAL replay and verify reindex outcome.
- Pre- and post-fix metrics comparison dashboards created: https://console.internal/redwood/dashboards/incident-ENG-98801

Runbook / Rollback:
- Rollback: revert router prefix change if increased error rate or trace regressions observed. Reverted change will resume prior behavior and requires immediate backfill for any new traces that landed in wrong partitions.
- Backfill can be paused if index pressure is too high; leave repair window open for follow-on runs.

Related artifacts and links:
- Incident notes: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/2026-03-10-regional-failover
- Canaries & metrics: https://monitoring.redwood/graphs?d=ENG-98801-canary
- Repair script: https://git.internal/redwood/scripts/repair/replay-metrics-backfill.sh
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123, https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/981

Stakeholders and customers affected:
- Escalation owners: Customer Success (Lena Carter), Solutions (Ravi Desai)
- Top impacted customers: "Acme Retail" (hosted), "FinSight" (Dedicated), two Private deployment customers (on-prem) reported partial telemetry gaps.

Acceptance criteria:
- All targeted tenants show restored time series with <=1% difference vs expected pre-incident baseline for the incident window.
- Trace stitching rate >99% for the backfilled window and no additional trace partition mismatches observed for 48 hours post-rollout.
- No increase in write error rate or index latency beyond normal thresholds during rollout.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Triage: Issue opened after multiple customer escalations. Logged noisy SLOs and partial dashboards. Assigned to Marco Silva. (Anika)
2026-03-10 - Investigations: Confirmed missing series correlate to tenant moves during failover; started capturing WAL excerpts and ingestion logs. (Marco)
2026-03-11 - Discovery: Found router prefix-cache eviction race (repro locally). Created PR to add versioned prefix-map fetch and fallback. Deployed patch to canary. (Marco)
2026-03-11 - Canary results: Router patch reduced misrouted trace writes by ~95% for canary tenants; trace stitch rate recovered for canary. Preparing backfill plan. (SRE)

2026-03-12 - Backfill started: Running replay-metrics-backfill.sh for 12 tenants. Monitoring index write QPS and search latency. First tenant backfill completed, validated against pre-incident snapshot. (Marco)
2026-03-12 - Communication: Notified Customer Success and affected customers of ongoing repair activity and ETA. (Anika)
2026-03-13 - Progress: 6/12 tenants backfilled; trace-link reindex showing 92% stitch rate; continuing with throttled parallelism to keep cluster load stable. (Marco)
2026-03-13 - Next steps: Finish backfills, promote router patch globally after midnight window, merge tenant-move barrier tests into main. (Team)
2026-03-13 - Postmortem note: Will create full incident postmortem and schedule follow-up retro to improve failover test coverage. (Anika)
2026-03-13 - Links: PRs and scripts posted in ticket description; dashboards live here: https://console.internal/redwood/dashboards/incident-ENG-98801 (Marco)
